_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3 per GROK-SPEC-archetype-templates-2026-08-15.md + ADDENDUM v3, using the Boston v3 exemplar as structural ground truth. Sources: seattle/REVENUE-STACK-SEATTLE.md + seattle/CREW-COST-SEATTLE.md + seattle/AUTHORITY-MAP-SEATTLE.md + seattle/SPEED-RULES-SEATTLE.md + seattle/hub.json. CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields (_contract, _provenance, _internal, _guard) NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. D6' LOCKED: utilization-stack economics lead frame. Upside rows are never summed into base totals. SCOPE REOPENED (Jaideep directive 2026-08-16): the full hub.json network including the Lake Washington cluster renders — see _internal.scope. SECOND PASS (Jaideep-approved 2026-08-16): lake economics now render as a SEPARATE dedicated N45 lake-vessel stack (20-seat commuter configuration; N30 draft superseded 2026-08-16 — commuter corridors run the 30-seat N45) (section lake_vessel; source REVENUE-STACK-SEATTLE.md §8 + EASTSIDE-DEMAND-BENCHMARKS.md); the Sound-anchored N45 P&L is unchanged and lake figures never sum into it. Lake demand rows carry sourced employer headcounts (EASTSIDE-DEMAND-BENCHMARKS.md §1). fleet_phasing OMITTED: no sourced Seattle fleet-count plan exists in any source file (fail closed — do not render a phasing section or a full-build capital figure). No vestigial v2 'asset' section: this file was authored directly to v3; vessel specs live in navier_intro only. Seattle seat pricing is DERIVED, not a city quote — every committed-bundle line carries status `modeled` + fn5.

fn1.text: Experience, charter and spot pricing is benchmarked to Puget Sound operators' published 2025–26 fares and rate cards.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships. Headcounts are each employer’s latest published figures, a measure of nearby demand rather than ridership.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect posted harbor speed limits. Speed-rule relief appears only as a separately labeled upside, never in base cases. Local precedent: Rich Passage 1, a foil-assisted low-wake catamaran run at speed through a wake-sensitive passage after beach-monitoring studies; also a speed allowance granted to an electric hydrofoil service on Stockholm's Route 89.

fn5.text: Committed-seat pricing is a derived band, not a Seattle quote: 3.6–5× the region's $210/month fast-ferry pass, ~55–70% below a door-to-door ride-hail substitute ($59–125/trip), and roughly downtown parking (~$220/month) plus two ride-hail round-trips. The global program band applies.

fn6.text: Crew costs are benchmarked to published Seattle-area wage data with a buffer for wage growth to 2026. This is a union-shaped labor market — median wages match means — so no low-cost crew case is modeled; shift structure to be confirmed in an operations walkthrough.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, rounded to the nearest dollar; leg counts are implied by the fill rate, not separately scheduled.

fn8.text: The conservative case runs cash-negative by design — deliberately punitive fill assumptions shown for downside honesty. No payback is quoted for it.

fn9.text: Puget Sound passenger water transit operates year-round today. The N45 rides foilborne through typical Sound chop; winter operations are an operational planning consideration, not a modeled uptime benefit.

fn10.text: Lake Washington service is shown as its own dedicated-vessel case with its own economics — lake figures are never blended into the Puget Sound totals. A lake corridor advances only when 60–80 seats are committed on it, and seat pricing uses the same estimated band, not a Seattle quote.

fn11.text: Spot fares are estimated from published ride-hail averages for the same trips — about $48 Bellevue→Seattle and $57 Kirkland→Seattle — and are set to match or undercut a solo ride.

fn12.text: Boeing’s Renton figure is the plant’s last published workforce count (2019). Treat it as an order of magnitude, not a current headcount.

fn13.text: Lake Washington and Puget Sound connect only through the Ballard Locks — a slow, first-come queue, not a schedulable link — so the lake runs a dedicated vessel whose economics stand alone.

Commuter bundles are the schedule spine; experiences, charters and spot seats carry the payback against Seattle's structurally higher crew costs. layer_pricing_basis.committed_bundles_L1: DERIVED $750–1,050/seat-month (cons $750 · mid $900 · upside $1,050) — no Seattle canon. Derivation per stack §3: 3.6–5.0× Kitsap $210 fast-ferry pass; ~55–70% below Uber Edmonds→Seattle ~$59 (~$2,600/mo) / Tacoma ~$125 (~$5,500/mo); ≈ parking ~$220/mo + 2 Uber round-trips; within program band $650–1,200 and below Boston's $950–1,275 because Seattle's public comparators are cheaper. Status everywhere: modeled + fn5. Needs Jaideep sign-off flag noted in stack file.
layer_pricing_basis.spot_seats_L2: $30/38/45 per leg × 10/20/30% fill of residual seat-legs (2,464/2,112/1,936) — bounded by WSF walk-on $11.35 / Kitsap $13 WB floor and Uber $59–125 ceiling. Fill rates unproven; status modeled.
layer_pricing_basis.experiences_charters_L3: Experiences $55/65/75 pp (Argosy 1-hr from $45.70 → Waterways dinner from $89; whale-watch $155 shows premium headroom); charters $600/650/700 per hr (Seattle Water Tours $1,675/2hr ≈ $725–838/hr for 42-pax displacement vessel; pricing a 20-seat premium foiler just under SWT is conservative).
layer_pricing_basis.sponsorship_U1: $150K/yr fleet-level placeholder ÷ 4 vessels = $3,125/mo — Boston precedent set (Citi Bike, Santander, HealthLine, Barclays); no Seattle-specific precedent priced. Upside only.
layer_pricing_basis.overnight_cargo_U2: ~$350/run × 16 nights — Casco Bay Lines 2026 tariff ($0.108–0.162/kg ≈ $216–324 per ~2,000 kg run) + Dropoff 2026 medical-courier premiums. First Seattle clean classes: batch parcels/documents (downtown↔Bainbridge/Kingston/Edmonds), catering/event logistics; medical/lab specimens remain a candidate pending a named counterparty (fail closed — no Seattle waterborne specimen contract found). No seafood in the premium cabin. Upside only.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil, not a boat with a battery.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the chop for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional boats. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.
